items.h: Devontez Walker comes up with clutch TD catch Sunday night
items.s: Devontez Walker caught both of his targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 30-23 OT win against the Falcons. Walker only has four receptions in the season, but he came up with the biggest one of the game for the Ravens on Sunday night. With less than one minute to go in regulation and the Ravens trailing 23-15, Walker came up with a seven-yard TD grab from QB Tyler Huntley. The Ravens would convert the ensuing two-point try and eventually win in overtime. Walker had his moment in this one, but he's well behind multiple other receivers in the Baltimore passing attack.

items.h: Hauls in one pass in win
items.s: Walker caught one of his two targets for 19 yards during Baltimore's win over the Titans on Sunday. Walker managed to record his second reception of the season, as he continues to make a limited impact offensively even with Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve. Walker will look to be more productive during the Week 5 matchup versus the Falcons.

items.h: Devontez Walker (groin) off injury report for Week 3
items.s: Devontez Walker (groin) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 3's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. It looks like Walker will be a full go for Week 3, as he is no longer listed with the groin injury that gave him some problems earlier on in the season. He should play and will see more work than usual if Zay Flowers (hamstring) has to miss another game for Baltimore.

items.h: Low snap count in loss
items.s: Walker caught one of his two targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints. Walker saw 17 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver also saw eight special-teams snaps. Walker saw nearly half as many offensive snaps as LaJohntay Wester (31), even though Zay Flowers (hamstring) could not play in the game. The 2024 fourth-rounder sees most of his usage as a deep threat, but appears to be unable to get reliable snaps with the offense outside of those packages.

items.h: Devontez Walker Remains off Many Fantasy Radars
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Devontez Walker missed the Ravens' Week 1 victory over the Indianapolis Colts due to a groin injury. Still, he completed three full practices and shed his injury designation ahead of the Week 2 home opener against the New Orleans Saints. His fellow wide receivers are not as fortunate. The team's WR1, Zay Flowers (hamstring), is doubtful for Sunday's contest, and promising rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was placed on IR after Wednesday's surgery for a fractured wrist. Walker has primarily been on the outside looking in, but he likely will see an uptick in usage against the Saints as the Ravens enter Week 2 slightly thin at the position. Last week against…

items.h: Should contribute on offense
items.s: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Walker should have a role on offense in Sunday's game against the Saints, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports. Walker missed Week 1 with a groin injury and now joins an offense that's likely without Flowers and won't have Ja'Kobi Lane (IR - wrist) for at least the next four weeks. Veteran starter Rashod Bateman is the de facto No. 1 receiver, with Walker, LaJohntay Wester, Chris Moore and Elijah Sarratt all candidates for significant playing time as well. Walker was in competition with Lane this summer for the No. 3 receiver job alongside Flowers and Bateman.

items.h: Devontez Walker (groin) good to go for Sunday
items.s: Devontez Walker (groin) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints. To no surprise, Walker has received full clearance to play on Sunday after practicing without limitations all week. He is primed to see more work than usual with Zay Flowers (hamstring) doubtful to play for the Ravens in Week 2.

items.h: Devontez Walker (groin) practices in full again Thursday
items.s: Devontez Walker (groin) practiced in a full capacity again on Thursday. Walker was again a full participant at practice on Thursday, which means that he will almost certainly be available to make his season debut on Sunday. He will likely play a substantial role against the Saints with Zay Flowers (hamstring) trending towards being sidelined for that game.

items.h: Full practice Wednesday
items.s: Walker (groin) was a full participant at the Ravens' practice Wednesday. Walker appears to have fully recovered from the groin injury that forced him to miss the team's 41-23 win over the Colts in Week 1. The wide receiver will be a welcomed addition Week 2 versus the Saints after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was placed on injured reserve Wednesday.

items.h: Devontez Walker (groin) practices in full Wednesday
items.s: Devontez Walker (groin) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday. Walker logged a full practice session on Wednesday despite missing last week's game due to a groin injury of some kind. It looks like he will be back in the lineup in Week 2, which is great timing given that the Ravens will be without Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) and possibly Zay Flowers (hamstring) in their matchup against the Saints this week.

items.h: Walker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's clash with the Colts.
items.s: The wide receiver logged limited practice sessions throughout the week leading up to the game and entered the weekend with a questionable tag. Ravens coach Jesse Minter described the injury as "minor" Tuesday, per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, but it's at least serious enough to keep Walker out for Week 1.

items.h: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.s: Walker logged limited sessions throughout Week 1 as he attempted to clear himself of a groin injury before Sunday's game. While the wide receiver could not avoid an injury designation, Walker still may suit up for Sunday's contest if coach Jesse Minter gives the green light. If Walker is ruled out, Elijah Sarratt will take over as the No. 4 option behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja'Kobi Lane.

items.h: Walker (groin) was listed as a limited participant at the Ravens' walkthrough practice Thursday.
items.s: Walker continues to nurse a groin injury ahead of Week 1, logging his second straight limited session Thursday. The wide receiver will have one more chance to notch a full practice Friday before the team takes on Indianapolis in the regular-season opener Sunday. If Walker is unavailable in Week 1, rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane could see an uptick in opportunities in his regular-season debut.

items.h: Walker (groin) was limited at practice Wednesday.
items.s: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter isn't sure if Walker will be available for Week 1 versus the Colts, though his limited participation in Wednesday's practice is at least keeping hope alive. The 25-year-old appeared in 12 regular-season games for the Ravens in 2025, totaling six catches for 136 yards and three touchdowns. If Walker can't get on the field for the opener, it could mean more targets for Rashod Bateman.

items.h: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tuesday that Walker (undisclosed) is dealing with "something minor" but is uncertain to play in Sunday's season opener against the Colts, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com…
items.s: Minter didn't elaborate on the nature of Walker's issue, but is could get cleared up when the Ravens post their first injury report Wednesday. Though Walker's availability for Sunday is looking iffy, Minter said that he expects the third-year wideout to practice in some capacity this week.

items.h: Walker didn't participate in Tuesday's practice while tending to an undisclosed injury, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Per Giana Han of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Walker was in uniform for the practice session, but he was working out to the side and mostly limited to agility work. The Ravens will post their first Week 1 injury report Wednesday, when the nature of Walker's health concern -- as well as the extent of his practice participation -- will be revealed.

items.h: Walker caught three of five targets for 22 yards in Friday's 41-3 preseason win over the Commanders.
items.s: The five targets tied for the team lead on the night, but Walker didn't do much with the volume as three other Ravens had more receiving yards, and none of the team's three passing TDs went his way. Third-round rookie Ja'Kobi Lane has been the star of training camp and seems to have the No. 3 wideout job locked down, leaving Walker competing with the likes of Elijah Sarratt, Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester just to find a spot on the 53-man roster.

items.h: Walker recorded two catches on three targets for 32 yards during the Ravens' 13-3 preseason win over the Vikings on Saturday.
items.s: Walker's second catch of the game went for 27 yards in the third quarter and was part of the Ravens' nine-play, 63-yard drive that ended in an eight-yard touchdown pass from Joe Fagnano to LaJohntay Wester. Walker has logged five catches on six targets for 63 yards through two preseason games, and the 2024 fourth-rounder is competing against rookies Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt for the WR3 role behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. The Ravens will wrap up the preseason Friday against the Commanders.

items.h: Walker made a strong impression during the Ravens' spring practices, Jamison Hensley of ESPN reports.
items.s: The 2024 fourth-round pick reportedly stood out as a field-stretcher during OTAs and mandatory minicamp, aiding his chances of earning a role behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman (personal). Baltimore added wide receivers Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt in the 2026 NFL Draft, along with rookie tight ends Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas, creating significant competition for targets. Walker has nonetheless flashed big-play ability in limited opportunities, turning seven career receptions into 157 yards and three touchdowns, providing reason for excitement if he does manage to make a leap in…

items.h: Walker will face increased competition for touches after the Ravens drafted a pair of rookie wideouts in Ja'Kobi Lane (third round) and Elijah Sarratt (fourth round) in the 2026 NFL Draft, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic…
items.s: Walker seemed like the top candidate for the No. 3 receiver role behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman (illness) prior to the 2026 NFL Draft, but the third-year pro may now need to impress in a competition this offseason in order to secure more than a situational role. Through his first two seasons in the league, Walker has hauled in only seven of 11 targets, but he's made an impact on those limited touches, with 157 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Rookie tight ends Matthew Hibner (fourth round) and Josh Cuevas (fifth round) also represent added competition for targets.

items.h: Walker had six catches for 136 yards and three touchdowns on eight targets across 12 regular-season games in 2025.
items.s: Walker has a unique stat line through his first two seasons. He's had seven catches on 11 career targets, but those grabs have gone for 157 yards and three touchdowns. Five of his seven catches have gone for over 20 yards. Dating back to his rookie season, Walker's first three catches all went for touchdowns. While that efficiency is promising, it's difficult to take much away from seven catches in two seasons. Walker might still be a worthwhile target in deeper dynasty formats. DeAndre Hopkins was on a one-year deal in Baltimore this past season, and two pass-catching tight ends, Isaiah…

items.h: Walker failed to record a single target in Sunday's 24-0 win over the Bengals.
items.s: Walker was a complete nonfactor Sunday despite playing a season-high 61 percent snap share. The second-year wideout played 25 of the Ravens' 41 offensive snaps in the contest, the second most snaps among wide receivers behind only Zay Flowers (32). The spike in Walker's playing time came on a day when teammate Rashod Bateman (ankle) was inactive. Even so, the North Carolina product was unable to earn any opportunities against Cincinnati. Walker is not a consideration for fantasy purposes as the Ravens host the Patriots in Week 16.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.s: Though Walker didn't take an injury designation into Sunday after a groin issue limited his participation in a pair of practices this week, the second-year wideout will hit the inactive list for the first time since Week 10. The Ravens will go with DeAndre Hopkins, Tylan Wallace and LaJohntay Wester as their depth receivers behind starters Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman.

items.h: Walker (groin) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.s: Despite suffering a setback Thursday with his groin injury, Walker was a full participant in Friday's practice and was able to clear injury designation ahead of Sunday's divisional contest. The wide receiver logged two targets in last Thursday's loss to the Bengals but was unable to corral either.

items.h: Walker (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Walker downgraded to a limited participant Thursday after logging a full practice Wednesday. The diminishing participation indicates a setback and puts the wide receiver's chances of playing in Sunday's divisional matchup with the Steelers into question. The 24-year-old will have one more chance to upgrade his practice participation before the Ravens release their final Week 14 injury report.

items.h: Walker did not record a catch on two targets during Baltimore's 32-14 loss to Cincinnati on Thursday.
items.s: Walker played just 17 snaps on offense during Thursday's loss, with his decreased playing time corresponding with the return of Rashod Bateman from a two-game absence. Walker has caught one pass or less in seven of eight regular-season games, and both of his receiving touchdowns came in Week 2 against the Browns. The second-year wideout is unlikely to see consistent work in the Ravens' offense unless Bateman, Zay Flowers or DeAndre Hopkins were to miss time.

items.h: Walker had a 30-yard reception on his lone target Sunday against the Jets.
items.s: The second-year wideout saw a season-high 23 snaps as Baltimore looked to find a spark in Rashod Bateman's absence. Walker was only targeted once, but converted it into the Ravens' longest offensive play from scrimmage Sunday. He has caught all four of his targets this season for 90 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Walker's overall sample is too small to draw hard conclusions, but he has produced when called upon, dating back to his rookie season. Pending Bateman's status for Thursday's game against the Bengals, Walker could have a similar role in Week 13. If Bateman (ankle) is back, however,…

items.h: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Walker will dress Sunday against the Browns in the absence of Rashod Bateman (ankle), Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.s: Walker hasn't played since Week 5, but Bateman's injury will give the 2024 fourth-round pick an opportunity to see the field Sunday. Walker figures to fill a depth role, though he scored two touchdowns against the Browns in Week 2.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.s: Walker will be a healthy scratch for a fourth consecutive week, and he's unlikely to play Week 11 against the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 16 unless the Ravens require depth at wide receiver. Baltimore will go with five active wide receivers in Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, DeAndre Hopkins, Tylan Wallace and LaJohntay Wester in Week 10.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Miami.
items.s: Walker will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week, which leaves Tylan Wallace and LaJohntay Wester as the Ravens' depth options at wide receiver behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and DeAndre Hopkins. Walker's next chance to play is Week 10 against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 9.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.
items.s: Walker wasn't able to suit up for the Raven's last contest versus the Rams during Week 6 due to an oblique injury but is now clear of any injury designation. This season Walker has secured three targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns, with both scores coming against the Browns. The wide receiver will have to wait till Week 9 to keep building his case as a reliable depth option for the team.

items.h: Walker (oblique) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: Walker wasn't able to suit up Week 6 against the Rams, but now coming off Baltimore's bye he appears back to full health. He figures to resume handling his usual depth role at wide receiver during Sunday's home game against the Bears. Across five regular-season appearances so far, Walker has secured all three of his targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns, with both scores having come Week 2 versus Cleveland.

items.h: Walker (oblique) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams.
items.s: Walker downgraded to a DNP for Friday's practice, and his oblique injury is severe enough for him to not play in Sunday's home game. Walker has served in a depth role at wide receiver and as a contributor on special teams this season, which makes Cornelius Johnson and Keith Kirkwood candidates to be elevated from the Ravens' practice squad to the active roster, especially if Zay Flowers (shoulder) is also ruled out.

items.h: Walker (oblique) isn't practicing Friday, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Walker played through this oblique injury in the Week 5 loss to the Texans, but he continues to be bothered by the injury, and Friday's absence doesn't bode well for his availability Sunday against the Rams. Friday's injury report will reveal whether Walker has a chance to suit up Sunday.

items.h: Walker (oblique) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
items.s: Walker was active in Week 5 versus Houston despite the injury, but it still seems to be bothering him as Baltimore starts its new week of practice. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full before the Ravens release their final injury report of the week Friday.

items.h: Walker didn't play a snap on offense in Sunday's 44-10 loss to the Texans.
items.s: All 14 of Walker's snaps came on special teams Week 5 while Baltimore went with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, DeAndre Hopkins and Tylan Wallace as its options at receiver. Walker made a splash in Week 2 with two touchdown catches in a win over the Browns, but in the three games since, he's managed just one 34-yard reception on one target.

items.h: Walker (oblique) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Texans.
items.s: After logging a 'DNP' on Wednesday, Walker was limited Thursday and then turned in a full practice Friday, before heading into the weekend listed as questionable. With his active status confirmed, Walker will be among QB Cooper Rush's Week 5 receiving options, but with fellow WRs Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, DeAndre Hopkins and Tylan Wallace also on hand, Walker (who has a 3/60/2 receiving line through four games, with both scores occurring in Week 2) is a hit-or-miss fantasy lineup option.

items.h: Walker (oblique) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans.
items.s: Walker popped up on Wednesday's practice report as a DNP due to an oblique injury. Even with the questionable tag, he was able to end the week on a strong note with a full practice Friday, which has him trending in the right direction for Sunday's AFC contest. Walker has three catches on as many targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns across four regular-season games.

items.h: Walker (oblique) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Walker is recovering from an oblique injury that he likely sustained in Week 4 against the Chiefs. He has opened the week with a DNP-LP practice log, and Friday's injury report will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the Texans on Sunday. The 2024 fourth-rounder has three catches on as many targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns through the first four games of the regular season.

items.h: Walker (oblique) did not practice Wednesday, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: It's a new injury for Walker, who had his snaps cut in Week 4 against the Chiefs, as he played just four offensive snaps after having 20 total in Weeks 2 and 3. Walker is operating as a depth wideout and special teams player for the Ravens.

items.h: Walker failed to record a single target in Sunday's 37-20 loss to the Chiefs.
items.s: Walker was not a part of the Ravens' offensive plans Sunday, as the wideout played just four of the team's 54 offensive snaps in the contest and was held without a target for the second time this season. Buried on Baltimore's wide receiver depth chart, the second-year wideout should continue to face an uphill battle for meaningful playing time. Barring injuries, Walker should not be trusted for fantasy purposes heading into a Week 5 matchup against the Texans.

items.h: Walker caught his lone target for a 34-yard gain in Monday's loss to the Lions.
items.s: That catch marked the first reception of Walker's career that didn't result in a touchdown. Prior to Monday, all three of Walker's career receptions went for scores. Still, a 34-yard grab demonstrated Walker's downfield ability. Baltimore has a crowded target rotation with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews eating up nearly two-thirds of the opportunities, and Isaiah Likely (foot) potentially close to his season debut. Walker's snap share may continue to remain on the lower end even though he is showing some promise on his limited opportunities.

items.h: Walker caught both of his targets for 26 yards and two touchdowns Sunday against the Browns.
items.s: The second-year wideout has three career receptions, all of which have gone for touchdowns. That's efficiency. Walker played 13 snaps Sunday after not getting on the field on offense in the opener, with his first TD coming early in the third quarter when Lamar Jackson found him in the back of the end zone on fourth down. His second came early in the fourth quarter to put the Ravens up 27-20. Baltimore has a crowded receiver room, and it seems as though Walker, Tylan Wallace and DeAndre Hopkins are all battling for the No. 3 job. Walker is likely third in the pecking order among that group at…

items.h: Walker failed to play a single offensive snap in Sunday's 41-40 loss to the Bills.
items.s: Walker played 21 snaps on special teams Sunday and was not a part of Baltimore's offensive plans against the Bills. The second-year wideout remains buried on the wide receiver depth chart behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, DeAndre Hopkins and Tylan Wallace. Barring injuries, Walker remains far off the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Browns.

items.h: Walker recorded six catches on eight targets for 61 yards in Saturday's 31-13 preseason win over the Cowboys.
items.s: The Ravens sat all of their top skill-position players, setting Walker up to start. He continued to carry over the momentum generated by his strong practices during camp by delivering solid gains of 17, 14 and 11 yards Saturday. Both Walker's practice and game performances have likely pushed him off the roster bubble, and he may unofficially now be fourth on the wide receiver depth chart ahead of Tylan Wallace.

items.h: Walker made some impressive catches with the second-string offense during Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts, Giana Han and Jonas Shaffer of The Baltimore Banner report.
items.s: After missing a few days with a soft-tissue injury, Walker is back in action and continuing his push for a depth role. Reports out of Baltimore camp suggest the 2024 fourth-round pick is having a nice summer, although he'll still have a hard time moving any higher than fourth on the depth chart before Week 1 -- behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and DeAndre Hopkins.

items.h: Walker (undisclosed) is practicing Sunday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Walker was held out of practice Saturday with what was deemed a soft-tissue injury, but the issue appears to have been minor. That's great news for Walker, who has had a good camp so far and is pushing for Baltimore's No. 4 wideout role behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and DeAndre Hopkins. While Walker is in uniform Sunday, he's working off to the side and not taking part in team drills, per Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun, so he may need another day or two to get back to full participation.

items.h: Walker didn't practice Saturday due to a soft-tissue injury, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Walker has had a strong training camp and has emerged as a leading candidate to open the campaign as Baltimore's No. 4 receiver. It's not yet clear if he'll need to miss additional practices, but head coach John Harbaugh said Saturday that the wideout has put on "a lot of mileage" in camp, per Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun. Walker played in nine regular-season games as a rookie last year, recording one catch for a 21-yard touchdown while also contributing on special teams.

items.h: Walker was Baltimore's most consistent wide receiver during spring practices and appears to be the frontrunner for the WR4 job, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Walker was a fourth-round pick in the 2024 Draft and saw just three targets across nine regular-season appearances as a rookie, catching one pass for a 21-yard touchdown. Walker played just 57 offensive snaps across those nine contests and was sixth amongst Baltimore's wideouts in targets. The Ravens signed DeAndre Hopkins in the offseason and kept Tylan Wallace with a one-year deal, but Hensley believes Walker is positioned to leap Wallace for the WR4 gig despite Wallace posting an 11-193-1 line on 12 targets and 275 snaps last regular season.

items.h: Walker made one catch on three targets for a 21-yard touchdown over nine regular-season games in 2024.
items.s: Walker was a healthy scratch until making his NFL debut Week 7 against Tampa Bay. The highlight of his campaign was a 21-yard touchdown reception against the Giants for his first NFL catch in Week 15. The vast majority of Walker's work came on special teams, as he logged 153 snaps with that unit as opposed to 55 on offense. There is room for Walker to move up in the wideout pecking order in Baltimore, and he'll look to grow as an offensive contributor next season.

items.h: Walker is active for Monday's contest against the Buccaneers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Walker will be active for the first time this season after the Ravens selected him in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. The wide receiver will operate as a depth option behind the likes of Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Nelson Agholor versus Tampa Bay.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.s: Walker has yet to make his NFL regular-season debut. The rookie fourth-round pick remains behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Nelson Agholor, Tylan Wallace and Deonte Harty on Baltimore's wideout depth chart.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.s: Walker is a rookie fourth-round pick, but he's yet to make his NFL regular-season debut. Deonte Harty (knee) is also inactive, so Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Nelson Agholor and Tylan Wallace are the Ravens' only active wideouts versus Cincinnati.

items.h: Walker (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.s: The wide receiver was also a healthy scratch for Baltimore's Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Walker is buried on the depth chart behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Nelson Agholor, Tylan Wallace and Deonte Harty.
